question.text: Scenario: Vikram Patel invested Rs.5,00,000 in DEF Equity Fund on March 15. He submitted his redemption request for the entire holding on April 5 (a Monday, working day) before the 3:00 PM cutoff. The following events occurred: Event 1: By April 9 (Friday, with no holidays in between), Vikram had not received his redemption proceeds in his bank account. Event 2: He called the AMC's customer care on April 9 and was told the delay was due to 'technical issues at the RTA' and that the proceeds would be credited within 2 more working days. Event 3: By April 13 (Tuesday), the proceeds were still not received. Vikram sent an email complaint to the AMC. Event 4: The AMC responded on April 16 (Friday) saying the RTA has been instructed to process the payment and it should arrive by April 20. Event 5: On April 20, Vikram received only Rs.4,85,000 instead of the expected Rs.4,97,500 (based on the redemption NAV and units held). He was not given any explanation for the shortfall of Rs.12,500. Question 1 of 5: By April 9, was the AMC in violation of SEBI's redemption payout timeline for an equity fund?

answer.text: No, the T+3 timeline starts from the date the AMC processes the request, not from the date of investor submission

Yes, equity fund redemption proceeds must be paid within T+3 working days, so April 8 (Thursday) was the T+3 deadline — non-credit by end of April 8 already places the AMC in violation, and by April 9 the delay continues

explanation.text: The Logic: For equity fund redemptions the proceeds must be dispatched/paid within T+3 working days from the date of the redemption request (April 5, Monday). T+1 = April 6 (Tuesday), T+2 = April 7 (Wednesday), T+3 = April 8 (Thursday). If proceeds are not credited by the end of April 8 the AMC has already breached the T+3 timeline; by April 9 (Friday) the delay continues and penal interest is payable for the period of delay. The Trap: The T+3 clock runs from the investor's request (when submitted before cut-off), not from when the AMC processes it internally. Mislabelling April 9 as the T+3 deadline (instead of April 8) is the common error. Note: Source: NISM Series II-B (RTA Mutual Fund) workbook — dispatch within 3 working days from receipt; delays attract penal interest.
